title: Warm clementine and prune compote with yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Clementines, prunes, apples, honey, hazelnuts and Greek yoghurt are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a saucepan, a small frying pan, a knife and a zester are needed, and the techniques are simple.

works.reason: The quantities suit four, the 100ml of water plus the juice is right for a gentle 10-minute simmer, and the cubed apples will soften in that time.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is realistic for zesting, juicing, cubing the apples, peeling and slicing the clementines, and chopping and toasting the nuts, and the 10-minute simmer matches the cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears except water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm clementine compote suits a late November morning, and the clementines are central to it as juice, zest and slices.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit with Greek yoghurt and toasted nuts makes a proper breakfast with protein and only a little added honey.
